title: The Man Who Invented Cruise Control Was BLIND 🚗🕰️ #shorts

scenes.text: The man who invented cruise control couldn't see the road.
Ralph Teetor was blinded in an accident at age five, yet became a leading automotive engineer.
Riding with his lawyer, who slowed down while talking and sped up while listening, he wanted a car that held its speed.
His device sensed the car's speed and pushed back on the gas pedal at the speed you set. A lock mode held it until you tapped the brake.
Patented in nineteen fifty, it debuted on the nineteen fifty-eight Chrysler Imperial as Auto-Pilot.
Today, radar adaptive cruise keeps your distance too.
He felt the problem instead of seeing it. What would you notice? Follow EV Drive.
